agree.reason: The pitch faces the failed first campaign head-on, guarantees refunds and keeps the remaining need small ($7.50 a resident), so this reader would probably pledge; but it gives no suggested amount and no way to pledge.

honest.reason: Every figure checks out ($49,000, about 42% pledged, $2,000 more than last time, a 76-mile round trip), though calling all-or-nothing 'the same' promise slightly overstates what the brief says about the first campaign.

works_the_facts.reason: It derives the remaining gap, the per-resident share, the percentage already pledged, the comparison with last time's total and the round trip, each in a favourable true form; it doesn't work out the pace needed between May 1 and June 30.

right_comparison.reason: The alternative is shown as the facts support it: the Majestic stays dark and the nearest screen is a 76-mile round trip, set against a cinema that was still selling 180 tickets a week when it closed.

qualification.reason: The all-or-nothing condition names a date, a number and a consequence, but the roof hedge gives no dollar amount (up to about $X more) and says nothing about what happens if costs exceed $85,000.

objections.reason: The worry about another refund is answered well with the smaller goal, existing pledges and the refund guarantee, and the low per-person figure eases giving fatigue; the open roof-overrun question is left hanging.

fit.reason: It is a signed, concise crowdfunding pitch of roughly 320 words, under the 350-word limit, though it has no pledge link or instructions.
